_comment: Ask the program: every answer shown on the site comes from this file, nothing is generated. Edit freely. 'aliases' are other ways people ask the same thing; 'keywords' help matching. Entries marked _todo need Vincent's confirmation. Links are site-relative.

aliases: What is AI for Digital Transformation
entries.a: An Associate in Science in AI for Digital Transformation at Long Beach City College: six applied AI courses, no coding required, that stack into certificates and a 60-unit degree. It's built for people who need to use AI well at work.

entries.q: Do I need to know how to code?
aliases: Do I have to learn Python
entries.a: No. Every course uses no-code and low-code tools. The work is deciding what an AI system should do, testing it, and judging whether it should exist at all, not writing code.

aliases: What do I need before enrolling
entries.a: None. No course in the program has a prerequisite. Some have recommended preparation (AI 45 before AI 60 and AI 65; AI 60 before AI 70; AI 70 before AI 80), but that's advice, not a gate.

entries.q: Which course should I take first?
aliases: What order should I take the courses in
entries.a: Start with AI 40, AI and Machine Learning Foundations. The recommended order is AI 40, AI 45, then AI 60 and AI 65 in either order, then AI 70, then the AI 80 capstone. Since nothing has a prerequisite, you can also begin with whichever course fits your schedule.

entries.q: What courses are in the program?
entries.a: Six courses, 3 units each: AI 40 AI and Machine Learning Foundations; AI 45 The Fundamentals of Generative AI; AI 60 Applied Conversational and Agentic AI; AI 65 Applied Multi-Modal AI; AI 70 Human–AI Collaboration and Workflow Automation; AI 80 Applied AI Integration Studio, the capstone.

entries.q: How many units is the program?
aliases: How many units is each course
entries.a: Each course is 3 units and 54 lecture hours. All six AI courses together are 18 units. The A.S. degree is 60 units: the six AI courses, supporting courses, and general education.

Four rungs: AI Literacy (6 units, in development, expected no later than Spring 2027); AI Fluency (12 units, in development); AI for Digital Transformation certificate (18 units, planned); and the A.S. degree (60 units, approved March 26, 2026). The same six courses count toward each.

aliases: Can I get a Pell grant
entries.a: Only the 18-unit certificate and the A.S. degree are eligible for federal financial aid (Title IV). The 6-unit and 12-unit certificates are not aid-eligible on their own, though the courses in them count toward the aid-eligible credentials. For your own situation, talk to LBCC's financial aid office.

entries.q: What is the AI Literacy certificate?
entries.a: A 6-unit Certificate of Accomplishment made of AI 40 and AI 45. It's in development and expected to be offered no later than Spring 2027. It is not financial-aid eligible on its own.

entries.q: What is the AI Fluency certificate?
entries.a: A 12-unit Certificate of Achievement: AI 40, AI 45, AI 60 and AI 65. It's transcripted and currently in development (moving through curriculum review). It is not financial-aid eligible on its own.
An 18-unit Certificate of Achievement made of all six AI courses. It's planned, transcripted, and it is the financial-aid eligible certificate.

entries.q: What does the A.S. degree require?
aliases: What is in the associate degree
entries.a: The A.S. is 60 units: the six AI courses (18 units), supporting courses, and 15 units of general education. Supporting courses with outlines on file are COSP 38 Database Concepts, CS 31 Introduction to Computer Science (Python), and COSN 250 Cloud Computing in AWS. The full approved list is in the LBCC catalog. The degree was approved by the Chancellor's Office on March 26, 2026.

aliases: Does it transfer to a university
entries.a: Where a course transfers, it is CSU transferable. Transfer records are still being aligned, so ask a counselor about your specific plan before counting on it. The program does not advertise UC transfer.

aliases: Can I finish in a year
entries.a: It depends on how many courses you take per term. The six AI courses are 18 units; taking two a term covers them in three terms. The full 60-unit degree also includes supporting courses and general education.
Grading is student choice: a letter grade or pass/no pass, chosen by the student.

entries.q: Are classes online or in person?
entries.a: That varies by term. Check the LBCC class schedule for the current offerings, or ask the program lead through the request-info form.

entries.q: I'm already an LBCC student. Can I add these courses?
aliases: Can I take a single course
entries.a: Yes. Any of the six courses can be taken on its own, with no prerequisites, and each counts toward the certificates and degree if you continue. Ask a counselor to add it to your education plan.

entries.q: Is this for beginners and career changers?
entries.a: Yes. The program is built for working adults, career changers, and students who want an applied credential they can stack over time. No technical background is assumed.
No-code and low-code AI tools, chosen by the instructor each term. Each course page lists examples of the kinds of tools used.

AI 80, Applied AI Integration Studio. Alone or in a team, students take a real problem, design an integrated AI solution, build a working prototype with no-code tools, and present it with documentation and analytics for workforce or community impact.
Yes. Every course ends in concrete deliverables, AI 60 and AI 65 end in portfolio projects, and the capstone ends in a deployed, documented prototype and a presentation.

entries.q: What jobs does this prepare me for?
entries.a: Roles where someone must evaluate AI tools, direct generative systems, build assistants and agents, produce multi-modal deliverables, automate workflows with human oversight, and deliver an integrated solution, across business, marketing, education and healthcare. The employers page describes what graduates can do.

entries.q: How does the program handle AI ethics?
entries.a: Ethics comes first in every course: bias and fairness, privacy and consent, and human oversight. The program's stance: the question isn't whether AI can do it, but whether it should, who it affects, and who's accountable when it's wrong.
Prof. Vincent Calip is the faculty author and program lead, in the Computer & Office Studies department at Long Beach City College. Department Head: Miriam Lynch. School Dean: Koby Moridzadeh.
Use the request-info form, which goes straight to the program lead, or email vcalip@lbcc.edu.
AI 40, AI and Machine Learning Foundations: what AI and machine learning are, where they show up at work, and how to evaluate a tool before you trust it. Your starting point. Formerly COSA 55.
AI 45, The Fundamentals of Generative AI: how generative models work in plain terms, advanced prompt engineering, and the ethics of bias and data privacy. Formerly COSA 60.

AI 60, Applied Conversational and Agentic AI: build assistants and agents that do things, not just answer, using no-code platforms. Ends in a deployed portfolio project. Recommended preparation: AI 45. Formerly COSA 65.

AI 65, Applied Multi-Modal AI: text, images, audio and video working together in real deliverables such as captioning, cross-modal search and voice assistants. Recommended preparation: AI 45. Formerly COSA 67.

AI 70, Human–AI Collaboration and Workflow Automation: automate real work while keeping a person accountable, with task design, agent orchestration, retrieval-augmented generation and human-in-the-loop evaluation. Recommended preparation: AI 60. Formerly COSA 69.
AI 80, Applied AI Integration Studio, the capstone: scope a real problem, build a complete AI solution, and present it to people who could hire you. Recommended preparation: AI 70. Formerly COSA 75.
Plan code 2150. Control number 46279. CIP 11.0102. TOP 070210. Approved by the Chancellor's Office on March 26, 2026.
AI 40, then AI 45, then AI 60 and AI 65 in either order, then AI 70, then AI 80. None has a prerequisite; recommended preparation is advisory.

entries.q: Which certificate does each course count toward?
entries.a: AI 40 and AI 45 count toward AI Literacy; AI 60 and AI 65 complete AI Fluency; AI 70 and AI 80 complete the 18-unit certificate. All six count toward the degree.

entries.q: What is the recommended preparation for each course?
entries.a: AI 40: none. AI 45: none. AI 60: AI 45. AI 65: AI 45. AI 70: AI 60. AI 80: AI 70. These are advisories, not prerequisites.

entries.q: Where are the course outlines and catalog?
entries.a: Official catalog information lives in the LBCC online catalog. Where this site and the catalog differ, the catalog is authoritative.

entries.q: What were the old COSA course numbers?
entries.a: AI 40 was COSA 55; AI 45 was COSA 60; AI 60 was COSA 65; AI 65 was COSA 67; AI 70 was COSA 69; AI 80 was COSA 75. Use the AI numbers going forward.

Evaluate AI tools; prompt and direct generative systems; build assistants and agents on no-code platforms; produce multi-modal deliverables; automate workflows with human oversight; and scope and deliver an integrated solution with documentation. They are not programmers; they are the people on a team who can put AI to work responsibly.

entries.q: How do I join the advisory board?
entries.a: The advisory board reviews what the program teaches, which tools it uses, and what the workforce needs next. If you hire for roles that touch AI, or expect to, ask to join through the request-info form.

entries.q: Can we bring a project or offer an internship?
entries.a: Yes. Students in AI 60, AI 65, AI 70 and the capstone build for real problems: a workflow to automate, a service that needs an assistant, a document set that needs a grounded question-answering tool. Internships and work-based learning placements are welcome too.

entries.q: What does the Experience button do?
entries.a: It turns on ambient sound, richer visuals, and hands-free control of the map using your camera: point to move the cursor, pinch to select, push or pull your palm to travel, turn your head to tilt. Video stays on your device and is never recorded or sent anywhere. It's optional; the mouse, keyboard and touch always work.

entries.q: How do I use the map?
aliases: How does the home page work
entries.a: Click any point to travel to it. Scroll, use the arrow keys, or swipe to move through the six courses in order; scroll back to return. Credential and page nodes are there to click. Every page is also reachable from the menu.
